# Halo+

> Halo+ is an independent planner for Grand Canyon University (GCU) students who use Halo, GCU's learning platform. It reads a student's Halo classes, assignments, due dates, grades and announcements and shows them on one screen that says what to do next. Halo+ is an independent planner made by a student. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Grand Canyon University. Halo is GCU’s learning platform.

Website: https://haloplus.app/

## What it does

- Pulls every class's assignments, discussion questions (DQs), quizzes and due dates from Halo into one list, ranked by due date, time it takes and points.
- Reads every class announcement and puts what it asks for (a moved date, a required format, something to bring) on the assignment it is about, in the professor's words.
- Shows Halo's real grades for every class and what the student needs on the rest of the term.
- A private calendar link that puts every due date in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook and keeps it up to date (on Max).
- Reminders and notifications for what is due; works on iPhone, iPad, Android and computers as a Home Screen web app.
- Study tools (on the Max plan): Practice (study plans, worksheets with answers, quiz me, flashcards from your class material), and Check your work against the rubric.
- On Halo's own pages (the Chrome extension, every plan): search across classes (Ctrl/⌘+K), one calendar for all classes, what's next and the grade on every class card, the rubric right on the assignment, and more.

## How it connects to Halo

- The Halo+ Chrome extension (the main way) runs on Halo's own page while the student is logged in to halo.gcu.edu and never sees or asks for the GCU password. On every plan it syncs whenever the student is on Halo, and any time they press Sync now. On Max it also syncs on its own every 3 hours while Chrome is open. On a phone or in a browser without the extension, a bookmark ("Sync Halo") does the same sync by hand.
- The first sync and the extension's own syncs apply on their own, with a note that says what changed and an Undo; anything that would remove an item waits for the student's review, and a bookmark sync is shown for review first. Assignments are still submitted in Halo; Halo+ only plans.
- Source code is public: https://github.com/richardsgeorger-collab/school-dashboard

## Plans (US dollars)

- Free: $0. Everything on Halo's pages (the Chrome extension), syncing whenever you're on Halo or any time with Sync now: due dates, points, grades and the GPA, Now, Calendar, Classes. No announcement reading.
- Max: $0.99 a month. Every announcement read for you (hidden due dates, moved dates, extra steps), auto-sync every 3 hours even when you're not on Halo, reminders and the Sunday preview, the calendar feed, and the AI study tools.
- Every new account gets Max free for 7 days of use, no card: a day counts when you open Halo+, from your first sync, for up to 30 days. A friend link gives both people extra free time.

## Help pages

- [How to see all your GCU Halo due dates in one place](https://haloplus.app/help/gcu-halo-due-dates/): Halo lists due dates class by class. Here is how to get every GCU assignment, DQ and quiz on one list, by hand or with a tool.
- [Halo announcements: how not to miss what your professor asks for](https://haloplus.app/help/halo-announcements/): At GCU, professors often put real requirements in Halo announcements. How to find them, what to look for, and how to keep up.
- [GCU Halo calendar: getting your assignments into Google or Apple Calendar](https://haloplus.app/help/halo-calendar-export/): How to get GCU Halo due dates into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook: by hand, with an .ics export, and what each way misses.
- [Halo GCU app for iPhone and iPad: what works](https://haloplus.app/help/halo-app-iphone-ipad/): Using GCU Halo on an iPhone or iPad: the browser, adding Halo to your Home Screen, uploading files, and which apps to be careful with.
- [Halo vs Halo+: what's the difference?](https://haloplus.app/help/halo-vs-halo-plus/): Halo is GCU's learning platform. Halo+ is an independent planner that reads from it. What each one does, and when you don't need Halo+.
- [How to check your grades in GCU Halo, and what you need on the rest](https://haloplus.app/help/halo-grades/): Where your grades are in GCU Halo, how points-based grades work, and a simple formula for what you need on the rest of the class.
- [Is it safe to connect a planner to GCU Halo? Passwords and privacy](https://haloplus.app/help/is-halo-plus-safe/): What to check before you connect any app to your GCU Halo account, and exactly how Halo+ handles your password and data.
